title: It was a great week for innovation across the model ecosystem. We’re bringing these new models into Copilot, enabling it to take on increasingly complex work, from quick questions to delegated tasks and, increasingly, complete long-running jobs through Autopilots. [Read more]
summary: It was a great week for innovation across the model ecosystem. We're bringing these new models into Copilot, enabling it to take on increasingly complex work, from quick questions to delegated tasks and, increasingly, complete long-running jobs through Autopilots. Here's one fun example: using an Opal-powered Autopilot running on a secure Windows 365 Cloud PC, Copilot goes through a month of trail cam footage, finds every animal sighting, creates a highlight reel of the best clips, labels each one with the camera, date, and species, catalogs every sighting in a spreadsheet, builds a PowerPoint summarizing the findings, and shares everything in Teams for colleagues to review. This is the next frontier for Copilot: software that doesn't just assist with work, but can own and complete entire tasks that unfold over hours or days. Learn more about Opal, the technology powering one of these new Autopilot experiences (in Frontier rings now and coming to Copilot soon): https://lnkd.in/grsmeiNt | 308 comments on LinkedIn
body_markdown: This is a fascinating shift in what we expect from software. 🤖 What stood out to me in this demo isn't simply that AI can analyze a video. It’s the end-to-end execution. A month of trail-cam footage goes in — and the Autopilot works through the task by: 🔹 Finding animal sightings 🔹 Creating a highlight reel 🔹 Identifying and labeling the camera, date and species 🔹 Cataloging the sightings in a spreadsheet 🔹 Building a PowerPoint with the findings 🔹 Sharing the completed work with the team That is a very different model of computing. We traditionally tell software how to perform a task. With agentic AI, we can increasingly describe what outcome we want — and the system can determine the steps, use the necessary tools, execute the workflow, and come back with the result. The interesting question is no longer only: “How powerful is the AI model?” It is also: “How much real-world work can an AI system reliably complete from start to finish?” That transition — from AI that assists → AI that executes — could have a much bigger impact on the way we work than simply having a smarter chatbot. We’re watching software move from responding to instructions to taking ownership of workflows.
